title: OOP Advanced
intro: Learn the basic ideas of OOP Advanced in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Inheritance
items.text: Inheritance lets a child class reuse or extend behavior from a parent class.

items.heading: Subclass
items.text: A subclass is a class that inherits from another class.

items.heading: Method overriding
items.text: A child class can provide its own implementation of a method inherited from the parent.

items.heading: super()
items.text: super() is commonly used to access parent-class behavior, especially inside an overridden method.

items.heading: Multiple inheritance
items.text: A class can inherit from more than one base class.

items.heading: Duck typing
items.text: Duck typing focuses on whether an object supports the needed behavior rather than checking its exact class.

items.heading: @property
items.text: @property provides attribute-like access to a method, often useful for controlled or computed values.

items.heading: __str__
items.text: __str__ can customize the readable text representation of an object.

items.heading: Composition
items.text: Composition builds an object by giving it other objects as parts or collaborators.

items.heading: Abstraction
items.text: Abstraction focuses on the important interface while hiding unnecessary implementation details.

items.heading: Maintainable OOP
items.text: Focused classes, clear responsibilities and sensible reuse usually make object-oriented code easier to maintain.
